landing.hero.title_html:
Your workloads have secrets.
They shouldn't have to store them.
landing.hero.lede: Idira gives every application — legacy or cloud-native — a cryptographic identity, then delivers short-lived, scoped secrets it never keeps. Pick a path and watch the identity exchange unfold, live.
landing.strip.step1.title: Prove identity
landing.strip.step1.body: App hash, client cert, SPIFFE SVID, JWT, a native cloud identity (AWS / Azure / GCP), and more — the workload proves who it is.
landing.strip.step2.title: Get a scoped token
landing.strip.step2.body: A short-lived access token, limited to exactly the secrets this identity is allowed to read.
landing.strip.step3.title: Retrieve, never store
landing.strip.step3.body: The secret is masked at the source and used in memory for one request — nothing lands on disk.
landing.problem.title: Secrets sprawl faster than you can rotate them.
landing.problem.intro_html: API keys in config, passwords in environment variables, tokens copied into CI and baked into images. Every one is a standing target, every rotation risks an outage, and every kind of application solves it a little differently. The result is credential sprawl with no consistent notion of who is asking.
landing.problem.card1.title: Keys everywhere
landing.problem.card1.body: Long-lived credentials scattered across services, files, and pipelines — each a copy that can leak and never expires on its own.
landing.problem.card2.title: Rotation = downtime
landing.problem.card2.body: Rotating a shared secret means coordinating every consumer. So it doesn't happen, and the blast radius grows.
landing.problem.card3.title: No shared identity
landing.problem.card3.body: A VM app, a container, and a lambda each authenticate differently. Without a common identity, policy is guesswork.
landing.variety.title: Every workload is different. The answer has to fit each one.
landing.variety.intro: There is no single integration point across a real estate that spans decades. Idira meets each workload where it lives — from a WebSphere app on a VM to a serverless function with no host to install anything on.
landing.variety.card1.title: Established apps
landing.variety.card1.who: Java · .NET · WebSphere · on VMs & app servers
landing.variety.card1.body: No rewrite required. An agent on the host serves cached, rotated credentials locally, or the app makes a mutually-authenticated REST call to a central provider.
landing.variety.card2.title: Cloud-native
landing.variety.card2.body: The platform vouches for the pod. A cryptographic SPIFFE identity is attested and issued automatically, and the gateway authorizes by identity — no stored credential at all.
landing.variety.card3.title: Ephemeral & serverless
landing.variety.card3.body: Nothing to install. Use the identity the platform already issues — an open-standard JWT, or a native cloud identity (AWS STS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes) — and exchange it for a short-lived, scoped secret.
landing.solutions.title: Four paths. One principle: identity, not secrets.
landing.solutions.intro_html: Each demo runs the real flow end to end and shows it in the Idira Inspector — topology, layers of defense, and a live trace of every call. New here? Start with Secure Workload Access. These are a few of the paths — the platform also authenticates via OIDC, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, LDAP, API keys, mTLS, and combinations of them.
landing.family.credential-providers.tagl: Vault-backed retrieval — an agent on the host (CP) or a REST call to a Central Credential Provider (CCP).
landing.family.secrets-manager.title: Secrets Manager SaaS
landing.family.secrets-manager.tagline: Authenticate with a workload-native identity — an open standard like JWT/OIDC, or your platform's native mechanism (AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes) — then fetch a scoped secret over the API. These are two of many.
landing.family.workload-access.title: Secure Workload Access
landing.family.workload-access.tagline: SPIFFE workload identity — ephemeral SVIDs authorize access; no stored credential at all.
landing.mode.cp.label: Credential Provider
landing.mode.cp.summary: Agent on the host serves cached Vault credentials via the Java SDK. Four scenarios — authorized, invalid hash (authn deny), denied safe (authz), dual-account.
landing.mode.ccp.label: Central Credential Provider
landing.mode.ccp.summary: Client-cert REST call to AIMWebService: four scenarios — authorized, no-cert (authn denied), denied safe (authz), dual-account.
landing.mode.conjur-jwt.label: Open Standard · JWT
landing.mode.conjur-jwt.summary: Present a workload JWT-SVID — an open standard — to authn-jwt, then read a scoped variable. OIDC and other JWT issuers work the same way.
landing.mode.conjur-iam.label: Native Platform · AWS STS
landing.mode.conjur-iam.summary: Prove identity with the platform's own mechanism — here a signed AWS STS request (authn-iam) verifies the ARN. Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes authenticate the same way. Then read a scoped variable.
landing.mode.swa.label: SPIFFE SVID → gateway
landing.mode.swa.summary: Four trust scenarios: trusted, untrusted, unknown, foreign.
